item.title: Iceland’s EU vote: A nation divided over Europe
item.description: Security concerns, control over fishing rights and rising living costs are shaping Iceland's debate over whether to restart talks on joining the European Union.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Migrant tunnels in Lithuania direct suspicion towards Minsk
item.description: Lithuania's border guards have discovered tunnels through which migrants are trying to enter the country from Belarus. Analysts see them as a means to destabilize the country.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy makes first visit to Russia-friendly Serbia
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy is making his first visit to Serbia. His host, President Aleksandar Vucic, hopes to score points with the EU, while Zelenskyy seeks more arms from a country that remains Russia-friendly.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ceuta: Spain warns Italy it will reciprocate entry checks
item.description: Spain has told Italy it will impose entry checks on visitors unless Rome halts its controls by Sunday. Even though they don't share a land border, the countries entered a spat after the Ceuta border rush.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: How viable is the potential Iran-Oman Hormuz shipping deal?
item.description: Iran says a shipping accord with Oman is in its final stages, but analysts warn sanctions, security concerns and rival US-Iran goals could limit its impact.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing seeks legitimacy in Thailand
item.description: Bangkok rolled out the red carpet for the Myanmar leader, but experts say the former junta chief still faces major obstacles in his bid for regional acceptance.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ebola: Africa CDC plans to use vaccine for different strain as outbreak spreads
item.description: The head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control pledged to deploy a vaccine for a previous Ebola strain in the current DRC outbreak, with test cases indicating a potentially lifesaving level of protection.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Drought threatens power supplies in Danube countries
item.description: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Mata Hari: Celebrated dancer turns WWI spy
item.description: Mata Hari enthralled Europe's elite with her beauty and performances. Accused of spying during World War I, she faced a French firing squad in 1917.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Can UN chief's initiative kickstart resolution for Cyprus?
item.description: UN chief Antonio Guterres considers a resolution to the Cyprus issue to be vital for regional stability and has initiated a new diplomatic effort. What are the prospects for its success?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why Iran is sending mixed signals on talks
item.description: Trump says talks with Iran are underway. Tehran says it is discussing the Strait of Hormuz with Oman, not Washington. Analysts say the gap reflects competing political pressures.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Africa and the ICC: Why most countries are staying
item.description: A new wave of African withdrawals has swept through the International Criminal Court. Chad turned its back on the court after three junta-led states in the Sahel exited. But most African countries still trust The Hague.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: What's behind the Algeria-Morocco rivalry?
item.description: Morocco and Algeria have been at odds for decades, chiefly over the territory of Western Sahara. But their rivalry now extends far beyond the territory.
